articles.title: I Remember the Screenshot, Not the Conversation: Adding Windows OCR to YuGPT
articles.excerpt: Remembering part of an answer is useful when you can search your saved conversations. But what if the words you remember were inside an image? An error dialog. Part of a settings screen. A diagram you…
articles.body: Remembering part of an answer is useful when you can search your saved conversations. But what if the words you remember were inside an image? An error dialog. Part of a settings screen. A diagram you meant to revisit. If the words do not appear in the surrounding conversation, searching its text will not find them. A filename such as image.png offers little help either. This is the story of making “perhaps it was in a screenshot” searchable. I develop YuGPT, a Windows application for backing up ChatGPT and Codex history locally and searching across saved conversations. I have added image search and recognition of text inside images using Windows OCR to the Microsoft Store Edition. Text search and image search sit beside each other at the entrance. Some conversation titles are blurred.

articles.title: We tracked 62 major cloud outages since 2020. Here's what actually takes the cloud down.
articles.excerpt: We've been tracking 62 major AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Cloudflare outages since 2020 that have a public write-up. Each one has the provider's own root cause, the region, and how long it lasted. On…
articles.body: We've been tracking 62 major AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Cloudflare outages since 2020 that have a public write-up. Each one has the provider's own root cause, the region, and how long it lasted. Once you line them up, a few patterns jump out, and most of them aren't what people expect. Here's the cheat sheet. The 30-second version The median major outage lasted 6 hours and 8 minutes. Not a blip. A full workday. 55% were caused by a change or a bug. Config pushes and deployments (32%) and software bugs or automation (23%). Fires and floods are the minority. Power and cooling failures are rarer but brutal. 18% of outages, with a median of about 21 hours. 37 of the 57 outages with a known end ran longer than 4 hours. 16 ran longer than 12. Only 7 were fixed within an hour.
articles.author: Noah Grinstein

articles.title: The Reconnection Storm: How Naive WebSocket Retry Loops Melt Down High-Concurrency Backends
articles.excerpt: The Reconnection Storm: How Naive WebSocket Retry Loops Melt Down High-Concurrency Backends In distributed architectures and real-time systems, WebSockets are the de facto choice for persistent, low-l…
articles.body: The Reconnection Storm: How Naive WebSocket Retry Loops Melt Down High-Concurrency Backends In distributed architectures and real-time systems, WebSockets are the de facto choice for persistent, low-latency, bidirectional communication. However, engineering client-side reconnection routines involves subtle distributed systems trade-offs that are frequently underestimated. When upstream infrastructure experiences transient degradation, network partitioning, or thread pool exhaustion, poorly constructed reconnection loops can trigger a catastrophic Thundering Herd problem. Instead of self-healing, unmanaged retry storms can DDOS your own backend servers into total unavailability.
articles.author: PhenoX

articles.title: Stop Guessing Which Bit Changed. .NET 11 Prints Doubles in Hex
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: In .NET 11, double, float, and Half accept the "X" format and NumberStyles.HexFloat. You get the exact bits as readable text, like 0x1.3333333333334p-2, and you can parse them straight back. Th…
articles.body: TL;DR: In .NET 11, double , float , and Half accept the "X" format and NumberStyles.HexFloat . You get the exact bits as readable text, like 0x1.3333333333334p-2 , and you can parse them straight back. This ships in .NET 11, which went GA on 2026-11-10. Everything below was run on the .NET 11 RC 1 SDK. The bug that prints fine Every .NET developer meets this pair of lines sooner or later: double sum = 0.1 + 0.2 ; Console . WriteLine ( sum ) ; // 0.30000000000000004 Console . WriteLine ( sum == 0.3 ) ; // False So how far off is it? Decimal text cannot really tell you. It shows you a long tail of digits and leaves the counting to you. The old way to see the truth was to dump the raw bits: Console . WriteLine ( BitConverter . DoubleToInt64Bits ( sum ) .

articles.title: US duty rates are not numbers: parsing 747 rate formats from the tariff schedule in Python
articles.excerpt: The duty rate column of the US tariff schedule looks like the easy part. It reads like a percentage: 6.5%, 3.7%, Free. Try float(rate.rstrip("%")) on it, though, and it fails on the very first declara…
articles.body: The duty rate column of the US tariff schedule looks like the easy part. It reads like a percentage: 6.5% , 3.7% , Free . Try float(rate.rstrip("%")) on it, though, and it fails on the very first declarable line, and special-casing Free only gets you as far as cattle ( 1¢/kg , still in chapter 1). The Harmonized Tariff Schedule (USITC, 2026 Revision 22) has 19,926 declarable lines in chapters 1 to 97. A declarable line is one with nothing more detailed under it, so it is what actually goes on a customs entry. Between them, those lines use 747 different rate strings .

articles.body: SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.

The information is revealed through links allowing Grok Build users to share their apps with others. Grok takes steps to randomize the URLs so only people who know the exact URL can access the data stored there. A design decision by developers of the platform, however, completely torpedoes that objective and makes it possible for anyone to enumerate thousands of live Grok Build projects. articles.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
articles.excerpt: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an exoplanet that "disappeared" after seven years of observations.
articles.body: Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world.
